title_en: Several Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on the Temporal Effect of the Application of the Company Law of the People's Republic of China

articles.content_en: Article 1 For civil dispute cases arising from legal facts that occur after the Company Law comes into force, the provisions of the Company Law shall apply. For civil dispute cases arising from legal facts that occur before the Company Law comes into force, if the laws and judicial interpretations in force at that time have provisions, the provisions of such laws and judicial interpretations shall apply; however, if the application of the Company Law is more conducive to achieving its legislative purpose, the provisions of the Company Law shall apply in the following circumstances: (1) Where, before the Company Law comes into force, the convening procedure of a shareholders' meeting of a company is improper, and a shareholder not notified to attend the meeting requests the People's Court to revoke the resolution within one year from the date of its adoption, the provisions of Article 26, Paragraph 2 of the Company Law shall apply; (2) Where a shareholders' meeting resolution or board of directors resolution adopted before the Company Law comes into force is confirmed by the People's Court according to law as not having been established, and a dispute arises over the validity of a legal relationship formed by the company with a bona fide counterparty based on such resolution, the provisions of Article 28, Paragraph 2 of the Company Law shall apply; (3) Where, before the Company Law comes into force, a shareholder makes capital contributions with claims and a dispute arises over the method of capital contribution, the provisions of Article 48, Paragraph 1 of the Company Law shall apply; (4) Where, before the Company Law comes into force, a shareholder of a limited liability company transfers equity to a person other than a shareholder and a dispute arises over such equity transfer, the provisions of Article 84, Paragraph 2 of the Company Law shall apply; (5) Where, before the Company Law comes into force, a company distributes profits or reduces registered capital in violation of legal provisions, causing losses to the company, and a dispute arises over liability for damages, the provisions of Article 211 and Article 226 of the Company Law shall apply respectively; (6) Where a resolution on profit distribution is adopted before the Company Law comes into force, and a dispute arises over the time limit for profit distribution, the provisions of Article 212 of the Company Law shall apply; (7) Where, before the Company Law comes into force, a company reduces its registered capital and a dispute arises among shareholders over the corresponding reduction of capital contribution amounts or the number of shares, the provisions of Article 224, Paragraph 3 of the Company Law shall apply.

Article 2 For civil juristic acts related to a company performed before the Company Law comes into force, which are determined to be void pursuant to the laws and judicial interpretations in force at that time but are determined to be valid pursuant to the Company Law, and a dispute arises over the validity of such civil juristic acts, the provisions of the Company Law shall apply in the following circumstances: (1) Where an agreement stipulates that a company shall bear joint and several liability for the debts of an enterprise in which it invests, and a dispute arises over the validity of such agreement, the provisions of Article 14, Paragraph 2 of the Company Law shall apply; (2) Where a company adopts a corporate resolution to use its capital reserve to make up losses, and a dispute arises over the validity of such resolution, the provisions of Article 214 of the Company Law shall apply; (3) Where a company merges with another company of which it holds 90% or more of the shares, and a dispute arises over the validity of the merger resolution, the provisions of Article 219 of the Company Law shall apply.

Article 3 For contracts related to a company concluded before the Company Law comes into force, the performance of which continues after the Company Law comes into force, and a dispute arises over acts of performance occurring before the Company Law comes into force, the provisions of the laws and judicial interpretations in force at that time shall apply; for disputes arising over the following acts of performance occurring after the Company Law comes into force, the provisions of the Company Law shall apply: (1) For a contract for holding shares of a listed company on behalf of others, the provisions of Article 140, Paragraph 2 of the Company Law shall apply; (2) For a contract under which a material subsidiary of a listed company acquires shares of such listed company, the provisions of Article 141 of the Company Law shall apply; (3) For contracts under which a joint stock limited company provides gifts, loans, guarantees, or other financial assistance for others to acquire shares of the company or its parent company, the provisions of Article 163 of the Company Law shall apply.

Article 4 For civil dispute cases arising from legal facts that occur before the Company Law comes into force, regarding which the laws and judicial interpretations in force at that time have no provisions but the Company Law has provisions, the provisions of the Company Law shall apply in the following circumstances: (1) Where a shareholder transfers equity for which the contribution period has not yet expired, and the transferee fails to make full capital contribution on time, the determination of the contribution liability of the transferor and the transferee shall be subject to the provisions of Article 88, Paragraph 1 of the Company Law; (2) Where the controlling shareholder of a limited liability company abuses shareholder rights, seriously harming the interests of the company or other shareholders, and other shareholders request the company to acquire their equity at a reasonable price, the provisions of Article 89, Paragraphs 3 and 4 of the Company Law shall apply; (3) Where a shareholder who voted against a resolution of the shareholders' meeting of a joint stock limited company requests the company to acquire its shares at a reasonable price, the provisions of Article 161 of the Company Law shall apply; (4) Where the determination of civil liability of a controlling shareholder or actual controller who does not serve as a director of the company but executes company affairs, the provisions of Article 180 of the Company Law shall apply; (5) Where the determination of civil liability of a controlling shareholder or actual controller of a company who instructs directors or senior officers to engage in activities harming the interests of the company or shareholders, the provisions of Article 192 of the Company Law shall apply; (6) Other circumstances that do not materially deviate from the reasonable expectations of the relevant parties.

Article 5 For civil dispute cases arising from legal facts that occur before the Company Law comes into force, for which the laws and judicial interpretations in force at that time have already provided principles and the Company Law provides specific provisions, the provisions of the Company Law shall apply in the following circumstances: (1) Where the articles of association of a joint stock limited company impose restrictions on share transfer, and a dispute arises over such restriction, the provisions of Article 157 of the Company Law shall apply; (2) Where the determination of liability for damages for a company supervisor's engagement in prohibited acts such as misappropriation of company funds, illegal related-party transactions, improper taking of company business opportunities, or engaging in restricted competing business, the provisions of Article 181, Article 182, Paragraph 1, Article 183, and Article 184 of the Company Law shall apply respectively; (3) Where the determination of liability for damages for a company's director or senior officer's improper taking of company business opportunities or engaging in restricted competing business, the provisions of Article 183 and Article 184 of the Company Law shall apply respectively; (4) Where the determination of the scope of related-party subjects and the nature of related-party transactions, the provisions of Article 182 and Article 265, Item 4 of the Company Law shall apply.

Article 6 Where the legal fact giving rise to the obligation of liquidation occurs before the Company Law comes into force, and a dispute arises over liquidation liability, the provisions of the laws and judicial interpretations in force at that time shall apply. Where the legal fact giving rise to the obligation of liquidation occurs before the Company Law comes into force but, as of the date the Company Law comes into force, less than 15 days remain before the liquidation period expires, the provisions of Article 232 of the Company Law shall apply, and the period for the liquidation obligor to perform its liquidation obligations shall be recalculated from the date the Company Law comes into force.

Article 7 For civil dispute cases that have been finally adjudicated before the Company Law comes into force, if a party applies for a retrial or the People's Court decides to conduct a retrial in accordance with the trial supervision procedure, the provisions of the laws and judicial interpretations in force at that time shall apply.
Article 8 These Provisions shall come into force on July 1, 2024.
